name: store_flood
kind: service-axis measurement: (a) the SM store service of lane stores when N SMs flood at once (per GPC, whole card); (b) requests that complete sectors a previous request wrote in part; no workload-based fitting
question: (a) What does one saturated lane-store request cost an SM when N SMs of one GPC, one SM of every GPC, or all SMs issue the same flood at the same time? (b) Does the extra cycle per partly written line of v1 (fresh lines) remain when consecutive requests of the stream fill the same sectors and lines, as a GEMM epilogue does?
motivation: v1 measured one SM. Its partial-line term was not installed because cutlass_f16bf16_dense_tma_ws_00 (STG.E.U16, 16 B into each of 4 rows per request, the next request continues the same rows) runs at 5.05 cycles per request at SM level against 8 for the term and 4 without it (protocol.json addendum of 2026-11-13). Full-gpu cases whose epilogue floods lane stores on every SM at once remain 20-35 % fast after v1 ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/fg-over20/notes/NOTES.md): H100 cutlass_dense_cpasync_03-06 / 08 (hardware 9.4-10.3 cycles per 4-sector request at SM level, engine about 4), B300 CuTe-DSL software-pipelined GEMM and FMHA MLA (hardware about 42.6 cycles per 32-sector request, engine 32-36). The engine's shared write service: H100 l2_write 3964.95 B per ns (carried over, never measured on lane stores) and 663 B per ns per GPC (measured on TMA stores), B300 l2_write 8038 B per ns (carried over), no per-GPC write service.
probe: store_flood.cu extended. (a) --active-file <SM ids> as tools/microbench/tma_store_loaded/probe/store_dest.cu: a grid of one CTA per SM (dynamic shared memory sized so that one CTA fits an SM), a CTA takes part when its %smid is in the set, participants meet on a global arrival counter before every window, the window and stamps are those of v1 (384 stores per warp, a clock read every 8). Every participating SM writes its own 16-MiB slice of the destination (requests of different SMs never share a line). Sets from tools/microbench/tma_store_loaded/scope_sets.py: one SM, g1k4, g1k8, g1kall (largest GPC), ek1, ek4, ekall (every SM). W = 4 warps per SM. Geometries: full16 = width 16, stride 16 (16 whole sectors in 4 lines per request); line32 = width 4, stride 128 (32 sectors in 32 lines); row4 = the epilogue shape: width 2, lanes 8 j .. 8 j + 7 write 16 contiguous bytes of row j (j = 0..3, rows 4 KiB apart), fresh rows for every request. (b) on one SM, W in {1, 4, 8}: row4_refill = as row4 but request k of a warp writes bytes 16 k .. 16 k + 15 of the same four rows (two requests complete a sector, eight a line; 384 requests fill 4 rows of 6 KiB, each warp its own rows), and row4 (fresh) as its reference. Runs a and b, 8 launches x 17 repetitions, repetition 0 discarded.

controls.sass: as v1 (49 clock reads, 8 STG of the declared width between neighbours, nothing else in the window); row4 / row4_refill: STG.E.U16.
controls.timing: one-SM cells of full16 and line32 at W = 4 reproduce v1 (T = 15.9 and 63.9 h100 / 31.9 b300 cycles per request) within 5 %; runs a and b agree on the steady gap within 10 %; the number of participating SMs is recorded and must equal the set size.
controls.steady: as v1 (groups 33..48, the two halves within 10 %).

derivation: T(set, geometry) = per-SM service per request = steady group gap / 8 / W (control subtracted), median over participating SMs and warps; also p10 / p90 over SMs. Refill: T(row4_refill, W) against T(row4, W).

predictions_before_data.engine_today_shared: The engine charges every sector 32 B on the per-GPC (h100 only) and device write services. h100: device 3964.95 B per ns = 2002 B per cycle -> with 132 SMs 0.474 sectors per cycle and SM: full16 at ekall = 33.8 cycles per request (15.9 alone), line32 = 67.5; per GPC 663 B per ns = 334.8 B per cycle -> g1kall (18 SMs) 0.581 sectors per cycle and SM: full16 27.5, line32 64 (its own SM service binds first), g1k8 full16 15.9 (no limit below 10.5 SMs), ek1 (8 SMs) no limit. b300: device 8038 B per ns = 3956 B per cycle -> ekall (148 SMs) 0.835 sectors per cycle and SM: full16 19.2, line32 38.3; g1kall (20 SMs) no limit.
predictions_before_data.hardware_guess: from the full-gpu cases: h100 row4 at ekall about 9.4-10.3 cycles per request (2.3-2.6 per sector), i.e. slower than the engine's 8.4 (4 sectors x 2.11); b300 line32 at ekall about 42.6.
predictions_before_data.refill: row4 fresh on one SM: 8.0 (h100: 4 sectors + 4 partly written lines), 4.0 (b300: whole 4-B granules). row4_refill: h100 between 4.0 and 5.5 (the tma_ws_00 reading 5.05), b300 4.0.

outcomes_before_data.shared_install: If T at ekall and g1kall is explained by one capacity per scope (per-SM share = capacity / participating SMs, same capacity in sectors per ns for full16 and line32 within 15 %): install the measured lane-store write capacities (memory.shared_service l2_write_bytes_per_ns and, if a GPC limit shows, l2_write_gpc_bytes_per_ns; b300 gains the per-GPC field only if g1kall is slower than one SM), evidence experimental until the replay passes.
outcomes_before_data.shared_other: If the two geometries need different capacities (cost not per sector) report the table; addendum with the form before any install.
outcomes_before_data.refill_install: If row4_refill is below row4 by more than 15 % on h100: the partial-line extra belongs to a line that is still incomplete when the SM hands it on; rule and engine change are declared in an addendum from the numbers (W dependence included). If equal: the fresh-line term is general and the tma_ws_00 reading has another cause; nothing installed.

prediction_check: H100 replay (tracer -> convert -> engine) is possible for the one-SM refill cells only (a traced launch covers one cluster set): row4 and row4_refill at W = 4 within 15 %. The N-SM capacities are checked by the full-gpu 500 x 2 regression against main's baseline (fg-over20/full-g1) and by the per-SM epilogue time of the named cases.
not_allowed: No family / case / shape specific timing; no tuning a measured value to the full-gpu error; post-data changes of a criterion are labelled with their reason.

addenda.runs: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/store_flood/h100-v2r3 (table.txt; runs a / b equal; participants = set size in every cell, no launch discarded; h100-v2r1 / v2r2 are failed rounds)
addenda.text: T in cycles per request, W = 4. One SM / g1k4 / g1k8 / ek1 (8 SMs, one per GPC) / ek4 (32): full16 15.94, line32 63.94-64.9, row4 8.36-8.44 - no shared limit up to 8 SMs of one GPC and 4 SMs in every GPC. g1kall (18 SMs of one GPC): 22.70 / 88.95 / 11.16, i.e. 1.42 / 1.39 / 1.33 times the one-SM value for all three geometries: the GPC serves about 12.7-13.5 SMs' worth of saturated store flow, counted in the SM's own cost units (sectors + partly written lines), not in bytes or sectors (full16 12.69, line32 6.48 sectors per cycle). The engine's 663 B per ns per GPC at 32 B per sector predicted 27.5 / no limit / no limit. ekall (132 SMs): full16 30.78 (4348 B per ns; engine leaf 3964.95 -> 33.8), line32 344-355, row4 54.9-55.5: the partly written geometries are 5.4 and 6.5 times slower than on one SM while full16 is 1.9 times; their destination footprint (104 MB row4 / full16, 830 MB line32) exceeds L2 and a partly written line that is not in L2 seems to move through DRAM as a whole line (line32: 3112 B per ns of 128-B lines, the DRAM service) - the ekall partial cells measure L2 capacity / DRAM, not the L2 write service. Outcome (a): 'shared_other' - the two geometries do not share one capacity in sectors; nothing installed; form to test before any install: GPC write service in SM cost units. Refill, one SM: row4 fresh 11.75 / 8.36 / 7.72 at W = 1 / 4 / 8, row4_refill 8.00 / 8.03 / 7.59. Prediction 'refill 4.0-5.5' FAILED: completing the sectors of the same warp's previous request does not remove the extra at W >= 4. Outcome (b) as declared: nothing installed, the cutlass_f16bf16_dense_tma_ws_00 reading has another cause. What that kernel's stores really look like (job sectors, $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/fg-over20/diag/stg-*/stg-first.txt; cutlass_dense_cpasync_05 identical): lane l writes row l % 4 of a set of four rows 16 KiB apart (lanes 0, 4, .., 28 share a half sector), consecutive requests alternate between two row sets and the half written, so a sector is completed by the request two later - not the row4 shape (lanes 8 j .. 8 j + 7 on row j, rows 4 KiB apart, completion by the next request). Bound from the kernel: 512 requests per tile epilogue in at most 2585 cycles with one CTA on the SM -> at most 5.05-5.7 cycles per request, against 8.0 for row4. Protocol v3 isolates the differences.
